integrity: Geometric fixed loci, simple connectedness, and canonical-index inputs are attributed to originating literature; orbit topology to Armstrong, invertible-sheaf descent to the standard descent theorem. Review is not independent.
scientific_limitations: Coarse complex quotients of smooth Calabi–Yau generalized Fermat complete intersections in dimensions >=2 and composite cyclic order >=4, with the diagonal cyclic action of arXiv:2610.21752v1. Neither smooth-locus nor stack fundamental groups, full Picard groups, nor Weil class groups are computed. The fixed-point and canonical-index inputs are prior work; possible implicit older priority remains. Full torsion Weil class groups follow using the published quasi-etale class-group exact sequence, whose prior origin is credited.
title: Prime-support fundamental groups and Picard torsion of generalized Fermat quotients
